originality.rationale: Live checks confirm nearest priors are asymptotic/expository only. Crossref query for certified-enclosure/Rouche small-n tables returns only Newman-Rivlin 1972 (J. Approx. Theory 5:405-412, asymptotic zero-free/limit theory), its 1976 correction, Walker 2003 Monthly expository note, and unrelated zeta/eta partial-sum items — no per-zero Rouche-disk table with centers/radii, majorant inequalities, and replayable counts for s_n n<=16, and no maximal-Re/minimal-gap witnesses at this scope. DLMF full-text search returns 5 generic pages with no certified zero table. Internal Resultary nearest hit SCOPE005 certifies only a coarse annulus 0.30n<=|z|<=0.75n for 10<=n<=14 via one outer winding count; the candidate's 136 per-zero disjoint Rouche disks over 1<=n<=16 with individual m>M and count 1 plus Szego-gap logs and two extremal witnesses is a material extension (wider range, per-zero isolation, new invariants), not duplication or renaming. No prior publishes rational/interval centers with Rouche majorants plus gap/extremal enclosures at n<=16.

value.rationale: Headline claim is a rigorously established exact invariant of the canonical Szego object s_n(z)=sum_{k=0}^n z^k/k!: complete per-zero isolation (136 disks), plus two motivated finite-scope extremals — largest real part among all zeros n<=16 and minimal scaled Szego-curve gap |w_n|-1 — each certified by disjoint intervals with explicit witnesses (n=16 conjugate pair 7.726102197 +/- 7.924591875i; Re>=7.7161 vs <=6.9848; gap in [0.15838,0.16193] vs >=0.17017). Object and invariants were motivated before computation (Szego 1924 curve |ze^{1-z}|=1, Newman-Rivlin/Saff-Varga/Bleher-Mallison asymptotics, Iserles-Norsett stability calibration; published tables give only bare floats without enclosures or replay logs). Values were not known or mechanically implied, n<=16 is a natural scope justified as the largest range with disjoint modest-radius disks under cheap quadrature, and a future researcher can reasonably need the precise enclosures as benchmarks for validated root-finding, stability boundaries, and zero-free-region methods. This is an independently retrievable exact census + extremal datum, not a textbook restatement, parameter substitution, tiny unmotivated gain, or unexplained enumeration.
